What are electrical engineering's two broad purposes?
column2: Moving and converting energy; and sensing, moving, storing and processing information.

column1: How do you convert a battery's mAh rating to energy?
column2: Energy (Wh) = capacity (Ah) × nominal voltage (V); 1 Wh = 3600 J.

column1: Power of a link from energy per bit?
column2: \(P = E_b \times R_b\): e.g., 5 pJ/bit × 112 Gb/s = 0.56 W.

column1: Landauer limit at 300 K?
column2: \(kT\ln 2 \approx 2.87\times10^{-21}\) J per bit erased; practical logic uses ~10⁵–10⁶× more.

column1: Shannon capacity formula?
column2: \(C = B\log_2(1 + \text{SNR})\), SNR as a power ratio.

column1: Doubling bandwidth vs doubling SNR: which raises Shannon capacity more?
column2: Bandwidth: doubles C. Doubling SNR adds only ~1 bit/s/Hz at high SNR.

column1: Five ideas that unify EE?
column2: Linearity/superposition, frequency domain, feedback, abstraction, tradeoffs (PPA + cost + schedule).

column1: What does PPA stand for?
column2: Performance, power, area — the core chip design tradeoff (plus cost and schedule).

column1: 2025 global semiconductor sales (WSTS) and the two biggest segments?
Fabless vs foundry vs IDM vs OSAT?
column2: Fabless: designs only. Foundry: manufactures others' designs. IDM: designs and manufactures. OSAT: outsourced assembly and test.

column1: How should you sanity-check a TAM claim?
column2: Rebuild it bottom-up (units × attach rate × price) and compare with the actual market segment size.

column1: What is an abstraction in engineering?
column2: A simplified contract for a level of a system that hides internal detail so the level above can be designed without it.

column1: Levels of the abstraction stack?
column2: Physics → device → circuit → logic/block → chip → package → board/system → software.

column1: When is the lumped-circuit abstraction valid?
column2: When the circuit is small vs the wavelength (rule of thumb < λ/10), or line delay < ~t_r/6.

column1: Wavelength formula, and λ at 60 Hz and 1 GHz in free space?
column2: \(\lambda = v/f\); ≈ 5000 km at 60 Hz, 30 cm at 1 GHz.

column1: Signal speed on an FR-4 circuit board?
Define noise margins.
Why must a digital gate have gain > 1?
column2: To turn a merely valid input into a strongly valid output, restoring noise margin at every stage.

column1: How does noise accumulate in an analog chain of N stages?
column2: Variances add: σ grows as \(\sigma\sqrt{N}\); SNR falls by \(10\log_{10}N\) dB.

column1: Per-stage error probability for a digital decision in Gaussian noise?
column2: \(p = Q(d/\sigma)\), d = distance to threshold. Q(6) ≈ 1e-9, Q(10) ≈ 7.6e-24.

column1: Reflection coefficient at a termination R on a line of impedance Z0?
column2: \(\Gamma = (R - Z_0)/(R + Z_0)\): +1 open, −1 short, 0 matched.

column1: Why can a 1 V source produce 1.67 V at an open transmission-line end?
column2: The open end reflects with Γ = +1, doubling the launched wave (here 0.833 V); later reflections ring down to 1 V.

column1: What is the reticle limit?
column2: Max single-exposure field: 26 × 33 mm ≈ 858 mm² (High-NA EUV: 26 × 16.5 mm) — a driver of chiplets.

column1: Give three ways abstractions leak.
column2: Timing (wire delay, skew), noise/power (droop, crosstalk, CV² heat), security (side channels), reliability (aging).

column1: Which two learning techniques are rated high utility (Dunlosky et al. 2013)?
column2: Practice testing (retrieval practice) and distributed practice (spacing).

column1: What is the illusion of competence?
column2: Mistaking recognition of familiar material (e.g., rereading a solution) for the ability to recall and apply it.

column1: Interleaved vs blocked practice result (Rohrer & Taylor 2007)?
column2: 1 week later: 63% vs 20%, even though interleaved scored worse during practice (60% vs 89%).

column1: Testing-effect result (Roediger & Karpicke 2006)?
column2: 1-week recall ~61% with self-testing vs ~40% for rereading only.

column1: The five-step problem-solving protocol?
column2: Understand (sketch, label units) → plan (principle) → execute symbolically → check (units, limits, magnitude) → reflect (error log).

column1: Units of RC, and of L/R?
column2: Both seconds: Ω·F = s; H/Ω = s.

column1: Volt in SI base units?
column2: kg·m²·s⁻³·A⁻¹ (V = W/A).

column1: Why must the argument of exp() or log() be dimensionless?
column2: Because these functions are power series; adding terms like x and x² requires x to have no units.

column1: What is a Fermi estimate for?
column2: A quick order-of-magnitude check that exposes which assumption matters most.

column1: Why do spaced-review intervals expand?
column2: Each successful review increases memory stability, so recall takes longer to decay to the review threshold.

column1: Criteria for moving on from a chapter?
column2: Concept check from memory; ≥80% of [A]/[B] problems unaided; derive the key result blank-page; explain it in 2 minutes.

column1: In SPICE, what does the suffix M mean? How do you write mega?
column2: M (any case) = milli (1e-3); mega = MEG.

column1: Main SPICE analyses?
column2: .op (DC operating point), .dc (sweep), .ac (small-signal frequency response), .tran (time domain); .meas extracts numbers.

column1: Why does SPICE report a negative current for a source delivering power?
column2: It reports current flowing INTO the + terminal; a delivering source's current flows out of +.

column1: How does SPICE solve nonlinear circuits?
column2: Newton–Raphson: linearize each device at the guess, solve the linear (MNA) system, repeat; it limits junction-voltage steps to keep exponentials in range.

column1: Newton–Raphson update?
column2: \(x_{k+1} = x_k - g(x_k)/g'(x_k)\); near the root correct digits roughly double each step.

column1: What is a self-checking testbench?
column2: Simulation code that compares the design's outputs with independently computed expected values and reports PASS/FAIL automatically.

column1: Why can't processors be verified exhaustively?
column2: A 64-input-bit block has 2⁶⁴ ≈ 1.8e19 vectors — ~585 years at 1e9/s; use directed + random + coverage + formal.

column1: Double-precision machine epsilon?
column2: \(2^{-52} \approx 2.22\times10^{-16}\) — about 16 significant digits.

column1: Why is 0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3 False in Python?
column2: 0.1 and 0.2 aren't exact in binary; the sum is 0.30000000000000004. Compare with a tolerance.

column1: What is catastrophic cancellation, and the fix?
column2: Subtracting nearly equal numbers loses digits (1 − cos(1e-8) → 0); rewrite algebraically (2 sin²(x/2)) or use a series.

column1: What is a tapeout?
column2: Sending the final design to manufacturing for masks; after it, hardware fixes need new masks (months for a full-layer respin, weeks for metal-only from parked wafers) unless firmware can work around the bug.

column1: Name the main engineering functions of a chip company.
column2: Architecture, RTL design, verification, DFT, physical design, analog/RF, package/SI/PI, CAD, firmware/software, validation, test/product engineering, quality/reliability, operations, applications.

column1: Metal-only respin vs full respin?
column2: Metal-only (e.g., A0→A1) rewires spare gates by changing only metal/via masks (possibly including costly lower metals) — faster/cheaper; full (A0→B0) changes transistor layers too.

column1: Fab cycle time rules of thumb?
column2: ~1–1.5 days per mask layer; ~14–20 weeks for advanced processes (R-020).

column1: Latest IC/ASIC first-silicon success rates (Wilson Research Group)?
column2: ~30% (2010–2020) → 14% (2024); the 2026 study reports 5% but changed its respondent recruitment, so lead with the trend. ~49% of project time in verification; ~75% of projects behind schedule.

column1: Why does first-silicon success fall as chips integrate more blocks?
column2: P(all n blocks bug-free) = pⁿ: 0.98⁵⁰ ≈ 36%; each block must be ~99.9% clean for 95% overall.

column1: Why do plans built from most-likely durations run late?
column2: Task durations are right-skewed; means exceed modes, so the sum of modes is met well under half the time.

column1: Mean of a triangular distribution (min a, mode m, max b)?
Why are leading-edge design-cost figures (e.g., $725 M at 2 nm) contested?
column2: They assume from-scratch design with no reuse and include software/verification/IP qualification (~71%); critics say real costs are lower.

column1: Strong answer to 'what escaped in your last tapeouts?'
column2: Specific steppings, root causes and process changes since — not 'everything worked'.

column1: Why should verification be independent of design?
column2: Like an audit: checks written by the designer share the designer's misunderstandings and miss the same bugs.
